figure_description: A square is divided into 7 geometric pieces. A diagonal line connects the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner. Below this diagonal, a line segment runs from the center of the square (the midpoint of the diagonal) to the bottom-right corner, dividing the entire lower-right half into two congruent right isosceles triangles. Above the diagonal, line segments partition the upper-left half into five pieces: a square, a parallelogram, and three triangles.
